gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-switzer: Switzer draws tubular, wire-like letters with a tall waist line, and its c tips stay politely apart from each other. Rounded Elegance packs its warm monoline letters nearly touching; Switzer lets each one breathe.
gen-dafont-sansumi-fs-asap: Sansumi spaces out rod-like letters, flat in weight, like tick marks on a tape measure. Asap follows with open-arc c shapes and a lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals, so a modest size is plenty.
gen-dafont-sansumi-fs-epilogue: Geometric and neutral, Sansumi keeps a flat stroke and a first capital that barely rises above its neighbors, which looks best big and brief. Epilogue then loosens up, curvy and wire-thin, with stubby ascender tips on a tall-bodied plain sans.
gen-dafont-sansumi-general-sans: General Sans reads clean and smooth, its x-height filling the line and every bend left unobstructed by fussy detail. Sansumi stretches wide tracking across flat strokes, while General Sans is the one built for steady running text.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-rowan: Rowan reads literary and friendly, with generous openings in every curve and thin strokes about half the weight of thick ones. Starborn floats dreamy gaps between its letters above it, and that spacious display mood leads into the serif's gentler texture.
gen-dafont-stilu-fs-asap: Tall lowercase bowls like blown glass bulbs give Stilu its luxurious look, with terminals that never close in. Asap stays low and readable below, so Stilu belongs big and short.
gen-dafont-stilu-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads approachable and contemporary, curvy and unclamped, with a wire-like skeleton and stubby ascender tips. And since Stilu has similar tall, round lowercase, a modest size difference between them is enough.
gen-dafont-stilu-fs-nunito: Stilu's strokes keep one weight through every curve and straight, and its terminals never close in. But Nunito is the rounder one, with big lowercase bowls and terminals that finish well clear of the stem.
gen-dafont-stilu-general-sans: General Sans reads clean and professional, with steady pen pressure and an x-height that fills the line. And Stilu brings refined, luxurious glass-bulb bowls, leaving General Sans to handle the everyday text.
gen-dafont-stilu-switzer: Stilu's tall lowercase bowls look like blown glass bulbs, drawn at a single line width with terminals left open. Switzer keeps its c tips well apart and its tubular letters tall in the waist, so a long page stays light and approachable.
